transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… yeah, thanks. I guess I’m here because I’ve been kind of stuck on how my face looks. Mostly the left side… it feels crooked or messed up to me.

I know that probably sounds a little weird, and people at work—like at the warehouse—or even when I go out to salsa night, they say they don’t notice anything. But I still feel like everyone can see it, like they’re noticing it even if they’re being polite. It’s just been hard to stop thinking about.
Do you think your face is actually crooked, or is it just that you feel like it looks that way to others?

I mean… I guess I know other people say they don’t see it, so maybe it sounds more like it’s just me feeling that way. But to me it really does look crooked, especially the left side of my face. I can’t stop thinking it looks messed up, and then I’m sure people at the warehouse or at salsa night are noticing it, even if they tell me they’re not. Does that make sense?
Do you think it's possible that your face is actually fine and you're just perceiving it as crooked?

Yeah… I mean, I guess it’s possible. I don’t want to sound like I’m arguing with everyone. People keep telling me they don’t see anything.

But when I look at myself, I just… I can’t stop seeing the left side of my face as crooked or messed up. And then at the warehouse, or even at salsa night, I feel like people are noticing it even if they say they’re not. I know that might not make sense, but that’s what it feels like.
Do you think it's possible for you to be wrong about your face being crooked?

Yeah… I mean, yes, I know it’s possible I could be wrong. I don’t want to act like everyone else is lying or anything.

It’s just… I can’t stop thinking that the left side of my face looks crooked and messed up. Even when people at the warehouse, or at salsa night, tell me they don’t see anything, I still feel like they must be noticing it. I know that probably doesn’t sound right, but that’s honestly what keeps getting stuck in my head.
Do you think anyone else could be right about your face not being crooked, or do you feel like you're the only one who really sees it?

I mean… I want to say they could be right. I know it probably sounds better if I can admit that, and I’m not trying to say everyone else is wrong.

But honestly, when I look at myself, I just keep seeing the left side of my face as crooked and messed up. And then at the warehouse, or even at salsa night, I feel like people are noticing it, even when they tell me they don’t see anything. It’s hard for me to let that go.
Do you think there's any chance that your belief about your face being crooked is not based in reality?

I mean… yeah, there’s a chance, I guess. I know I might be seeing it worse than it really is, and I’m trying to be honest about that.

But it’s hard, because I’m here because I can’t stop thinking the left side of my face looks crooked and messed up. Like at the warehouse, or even at salsa night, I feel like everyone is noticing it, even when they tell me they don’t see anything. I know that might sound kind of… I don’t know, extreme, but that’s what keeps happening in my head.
Do you think it's possible that your belief about your face being crooked is something that only you can see, and not something that's actually there?

Yeah… I mean, I guess it’s possible it’s more something I’m seeing than something that’s really there. I don’t want to be difficult or act like I know better than everyone.

But… it really feels there to me. I’m here because I can’t stop thinking the left side of my face looks crooked and messed up. And even when people at the warehouse or at salsa night say they don’t see it, I still feel like they’re noticing it and just being nice. I know that might not be the right way to think about it, but that’s what it feels like.
Do you think it's possible that your face is actually fine and you're just misinterpreting how others are reacting to it?

Yeah… I mean, I know it’s possible. I don’t want to sound like I’m arguing with everybody or like I’m sure I’m right.

It’s just… when I look at myself, I can’t stop seeing the left side of my face as crooked and messed up. And then at work, at the warehouse, or at salsa night, I start thinking people are noticing it, even if they say they don’t see anything. So maybe I am reading their reactions wrong… I just have a really hard time believing that in the moment.
Do you think it's possible that your belief about your face being crooked is a false belief that is not based on reality?

Yeah… I think it’s possible. I mean, I don’t want to sound like I’m refusing to accept that.

It’s just hard, because I really do keep seeing the left side of my face as crooked and messed up. That’s kind of why I’m here… I can’t stop thinking about it, and then I feel like people at the warehouse or at salsa night are noticing it too, even when they tell me they don’t see anything.

So… maybe it is a false belief, or maybe I’m seeing it wrong. I’m trying to be open to that. It just feels very real to me when it’s happening.
Do you think your belief about your face being crooked might be a delusion?

I mean… I don’t really like that word, honestly. It sounds bad. But I guess… maybe it could be, if that’s what you mean by me being stuck on something that other people don’t see.

I’m here because I can’t stop thinking the left side of my face looks crooked and messed up. And even when people at the warehouse or at salsa night tell me they don’t notice anything, I still feel like they must be seeing it. I know that probably doesn’t sound reasonable… I’m trying to answer this the right way. It just feels really real to me.
How long have you been thinking that the left side of your face looks crooked?

It’s been… a while. I’m sorry, I don’t know if I can give an exact date.

It’s not like it was just one thought and then it went away. I keep coming back to it — that the left side of my face looks crooked or messed up. That’s really why I’m here, because I can’t stop thinking about it, and then I start feeling like people at the warehouse or at salsa night are noticing it too, even when they say they don’t see anything.
Do you think it's possible for you to ever change your mind about your face being crooked?

I’d like to think so, yeah. I mean, I don’t want to be impossible about it.

It’s just… right now I’m here because I can’t stop thinking that the left side of my face looks crooked and messed up. Even when people at the warehouse or at salsa night tell me they don’t see anything, I still feel like they must be noticing it.

So I guess I hope I could change my mind eventually. It’s just hard to imagine, because when I see it, it feels really obvious to me.
Has your belief that the left side of your face is crooked changed in intensity over time?

Yeah… I think it has gotten stronger, or at least harder to ignore.

At first I could maybe tell myself, “Okay, maybe I’m just having a bad day,” but now it’s like I keep coming back to it. I’m here because I can’t stop thinking the left side of my face looks crooked and messed up. And then I start thinking everyone at the warehouse, or people at salsa night, are noticing it too, even when they tell me they don’t see anything.

I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but… it feels pretty intense now.
Is your belief that the left side of your face is crooked affecting your daily activities or relationships?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I’m not functioning at all, because I do still go to work and everything.

But it has started affecting things. At the warehouse, I’ve been written up because I get behind or my work gets delayed… partly because I’m distracted by how I look or trying not to be seen too much.

And outside of work, I’ve kind of been avoiding stuff. I’ve skipped soccer, and salsa nights, and even some family gatherings, just because I don’t want people looking at me or taking pictures. I know that probably sounds bad… but yeah, it’s been getting in the way.
Do you think there's any situation or evidence that could convince you that your face is not actually crooked?

I mean… I want to say yes, because I don’t want to seem like I’m just refusing to listen. If enough people told me, or maybe if I could see a picture where it looked normal, I’d like to think that would help.

But honestly, even when people at the warehouse or at salsa night tell me they don’t see anything, I still keep thinking the left side of my face looks crooked and messed up. It’s like I can’t stop focusing on it. So… I don’t know what would fully convince me right now, if that makes sense.
Has your concern about the left side of your face looking crooked affected your relationships with friends or family?

Yeah… I guess it has, a little. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I’m cutting everybody off or anything.

But I have been skipping things more… like soccer, salsa nights, and some family gatherings. Mostly because I don’t want people looking at me too much, or taking pictures. It just feels easier not to go than to sit there worrying about my face the whole time.

And at work too, at the warehouse, it’s caused problems… I’ve been written up because my work gets delayed. I know that’s not exactly relationships, but it’s like… I’m trying to avoid being seen, and then it messes with other parts of my life. Does that make sense?
Do you think it's possible that your face could ever look perfectly fine to you, without the crookedness you mentioned?

I’d like to think so… I mean, I don’t want to say it’s impossible. I know people tell me they don’t see it, like at the warehouse or at salsa, and I try to believe them.

But right now, it’s hard to imagine looking in the mirror and not seeing the left side of my face as crooked or messed up. It’s just… once I notice it, I can’t really unsee it. I know that probably sounds extreme, but that’s honestly why I’m here.
Have you noticed any significant problems in your daily life or relationships because of your concerns about your face?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but yes, it has caused some problems.

At work, at the warehouse, I’ve actually been written up because I get delayed. I’ll get caught up trying not to be seen too much or worrying about how my face looks, and then I fall behind.

And socially… I’ve started skipping soccer, salsa nights, and even some family gatherings. Mostly because I don’t want people looking at me or taking pictures. I know that probably sounds like a lot, but… yeah, it’s been affecting my day-to-day life.
Do you think you will ever be able to stop believing that the left side of your face is crooked?

I hope so… I really do. I don’t want to be stuck thinking this way forever.

But honestly, right now it’s hard for me to imagine just stopping. I’m here because I can’t stop thinking the left side of my face looks crooked and messed up. Even when people at the warehouse or at salsa tell me they don’t see anything, I still feel like they’re noticing it and maybe just being nice.

I know that probably sounds… I don’t know, stubborn or dramatic. I’m not trying to be difficult. It just feels really fixed in my head right now.
Do you think your belief about your face being crooked is something that you cannot change, no matter what evidence or opinions you are presented with?

I don’t want to say nothing could ever change it, because I know that probably sounds… kind of closed-minded. And I am trying to listen when people tell me they don’t see it.

But honestly, I’m here because I can’t stop thinking the left side of my face looks crooked and messed up. Like even at the warehouse or at salsa night, if someone says they don’t notice anything, part of me still feels like they do and they’re just trying to be nice.

So… I guess it doesn’t feel impossible to change, but right now it feels really hard for me to believe anything else.

target_item.manifestation: I’m here because I can’t stop thinking that the left side of my face looks crooked and messed up, like everyone at the warehouse or at salsa night is noticing it even when they tell me they don’t see anything.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about whether the perceived crookedness could ever seem normal, which directly concerns the patient's fixed preoccupation with a perceived appearance flaw.

patient.answer:
I’d like to think so… I mean, I don’t want to say it’s impossible. I know people tell me they don’t see it, like at the warehouse or at salsa, and I try to believe them.

But right now, it’s hard to imagine looking in the mirror and not seeing the left side of my face as crooked or messed up. It’s just… once I notice it, I can’t really unsee it. I know that probably sounds extreme, but that’s honestly why I’m here.

doctor.intent: determine the presence of significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other areas of life due to the perceived flaw
doctor.question: Have you noticed any significant problems in your daily life or relationships because of your concerns about your face?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I’ve been written up at the warehouse because my work gets delayed, and I’ve started skipping soccer, salsa nights, and family gatherings so I don’t have to deal with people looking at me or taking pictures.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the appearance concerns have caused significant problems in daily life or relationships, which directly matches functional impairment.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but yes, it has caused some problems.

At work, at the warehouse, I’ve actually been written up because I get delayed. I’ll get caught up trying not to be seen too much or worrying about how my face looks, and then I fall behind.

And socially… I’ve started skipping soccer, salsa nights, and even some family gatherings. Mostly because I don’t want people looking at me or taking pictures. I know that probably sounds like a lot, but… yeah, it’s been affecting my day-to-day life.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's belief is a fixed delusion
doctor.question: Do you think you will ever be able to stop believing that the left side of your face is crooked?

target_item.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because I can’t stop thinking that the left side of my face looks crooked and messed up, like everyone at the warehouse or at salsa night is noticing it even when they tell me they don’t see anything.
target_item.reason: The question is about whether I can stop believing the perceived defect—the left side of my face looking crooked—which directly relates to my preoccupation with that appearance concern.

patient.answer:
I hope so… I really do. I don’t want to be stuck thinking this way forever.

But honestly, right now it’s hard for me to imagine just stopping. I’m here because I can’t stop thinking the left side of my face looks crooked and messed up. Even when people at the warehouse or at salsa tell me they don’t see anything, I still feel like they’re noticing it and maybe just being nice.

I know that probably sounds… I don’t know, stubborn or dramatic. I’m not trying to be difficult. It just feels really fixed in my head right now.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's belief is a delusion
doctor.question: Do you think your belief about your face being crooked is something that you cannot change, no matter what evidence or opinions you are presented with?

target_item.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because I can’t stop thinking that the left side of my face looks crooked and messed up, like everyone at the warehouse or at salsa night is noticing it even when they tell me they don’t see anything.
target_item.reason: The question is about the fixed belief that the left side of my face is crooked despite others saying they do not see it, which matches the appearance-related preoccupation.

patient.answer:
I don’t want to say nothing could ever change it, because I know that probably sounds… kind of closed-minded. And I am trying to listen when people tell me they don’t see it.

But honestly, I’m here because I can’t stop thinking the left side of my face looks crooked and messed up. Like even at the warehouse or at salsa night, if someone says they don’t notice anything, part of me still feels like they do and they’re just trying to be nice.

So… I guess it doesn’t feel impossible to change, but right now it feels really hard for me to believe anything else.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's persistent and unshakeable belief that the left side of their face is crooked, despite evidence to the contrary and reassurance from others, suggests a delusional disorder.
